title: TAX ACCOUNTING
hours: 4 hours per week: (4.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours/ 0.00 activity hours)
description: Presents current Federal and California income tax law as it relates to individuals, emphasizing practical application, tax planning and tax form preparation. Introduces the principles of accounting as related to income tax preparation.

title: ELEMENTS OF ACCOUNTING FOR BUSINESS INCLUDING AGRICULTURAL BUSINESS
hours: 4 hours per week: (4.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours/ 0.00 activity hours)
description: Provides a study of the principles of accounting for small business including agricultural business. Principles include types of records required, their use and how to compute and use measures of earnings and cost of production to improve business and agribusiness efficiencies. Income tax, Social Security, and employee payroll records also included. Application of these concepts and methods will include hands-on projects to develop computer-based solutions for a business or agribusiness. Students will choose a business focus from agricultural, service or retail merchandiser businesses.

title: COMPUTERIZED ACCOUNTING - QUICKBOOKS I
hours: 2 hours per week: (2.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours/ 0.00 activity hours)
description: Provides students with the knowledge, skills, and practice needed to use microcomputers for accounting applications. Includes inputting and electronically managing general journal, specialized journals, financial statement analysis, payroll, inventory, accounts receivable, accounts payable, depreciation, and other accounting applications. Provides training for entry-level computerized bookkeepers, small business owners, and students pursuing further accounting courses.

title: COMPUTERIZED ACCOUNTING - QUICKBOOKS II
hours: 2 hours per week: (2.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours/ 0.00 activity hours)
description: Expands upon the knowledge of using Quickbooks for more advanced reporting, including inventory management, payroll, and financial reports.

title: WORK EXPERIENCE IN ACCOUNTING
hours: 1.5 to 12 hours per week: (0.00 - 0.00 lecture hours/ 0.00 - 0.00 lab hours/1.50 - 12.00 work experience hours)
description: Provides opportunities for students in Accounting to connect academic curricula to experiential learning in the workplace as an internship, Service Learning placement or general employment. Allows students to develop and work on learning objectives in workplace competencies and technical skills relevant for their course of study and career pathway. Students must work 54 hours for each unit of credit earned, in half-unit increments (27 hours), up to a maximum of 4 units. Employment can be paid or unpaid.

title: ASHS SPECIAL TOPIC
hours: 1.5 to 12 hours per week: (0.00 - 0.00 lecture hours/ 1.50 - 12.00 lab hours)
description: Examines a special topic in the field of study related to the discipline offering this course.

title: LIFE MANAGEMENT
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Articulates skills to understand and utilize internal and external resources to function effectively in contemporary US society. Major topics include socio-cultural forces that affect personal values, beliefs, behaviors and goal setting; decision-making strategies, time management and stress-reduction strategies; and conflict resolution methods. Strategies and skills for improving self-esteem, selfcare, self-understanding, and interpersonal relationships are also introduced.

title: INTRODUCTION TO SOCIAL WORK AND HUMAN SERVICES
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Examines an introductory overview of U.S. social welfare, social work, and social institutions that deliver the provision of human support services. Presents a historical perspective on the development of the U.S. social work and human services profession with emphasis on delivery systems and protocols. Particular attention is given to policies and procedures that uphold antiracism and social equity practices that support individual and family holistic functioning.

title: HUMAN DEVELOPMENT: LIFE SPAN
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours/ 0.00 activity hours)
description: Integrates the physical, social, emotional and cognitive aspects of human development throughout the lifespan. Discusses the developmental tasks facing people at various points in the life cycle. Explores the way social interaction and cultural institutions shape the development of the individual. Meets Title XXII requirements: DS 1.

title: FAMILY, RELATIONSHIPS AND INTIMACY
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Focuses on diversity within and the development of committed relationships and the family unit. Emphasizes intimacy dynamics, communication processes, and assessment of functionality and wellness.

title: HUMAN SEXUALITY: EXPERIENCE & EXPRESSION
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Studies the complex psychological, sociological and physiological aspects of human sexuality. Introduces theoretical frameworks that explain sexual development and identity; sexual behaviors; gendered patterns and gender roles; and sexual satisfaction. Examines the societal constructions that define ab/normal sexual expression and the changing definitions of subjective experiences. Discusses sexual response processes, dysfunctions, reproductive health, and sexual violence and healing pathways.

title: INDEPENDENT STUDIES: HUMANDEVELOPMENT/HUMAN SERVICES
hours: 1.5 to 6 hours per week: (0.00 - 0.00 lecture hours/ 1.50 - 6.00 lab hours)
prereqs: The student must have completed preparatory course work in the field in which the study is to be undertaken.
description: Provides an opportunity for an in-depth study or a practicum experience by an individual student in a selected topic of human development/human services under the direction of an instructor.

title: WORK EXPERIENCE IN HUMAN SERVICES
hours: 1.5 to 12 hours per week: (0.00 - 0.00 lecture hours/ 0.00 - 0.00 lab hours/1.50 - 12.00 work experience hours)
description: Provides opportunities for students in Human Services to connect academic curricula to experiential learning in the workplace as an internship, Service Learning placement or general employment. Allows students to develop and work on learning objectives in workplace competencies and technical skills relevant for their course of study and career pathway. Students must work 54 hours for each unit of credit earned, in half-unit increments (27 hours), up to a maximum of 4 units. Employment can be paid or unpaid. Repeatable: 3 Times

title: CHICANX AND LATINX COMMUNITY PRACTICE
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Examines historical and contemporary efforts to address patterns of inequities affecting Chicanx and Latinx communities. Introduces key concepts for understanding equity, policy change, and community wellbeing among Chicanx and Latinx communities. Covers intergenerational trauma, medical exploitation, eugenics, intersectional disparities, barriers to accessing care, Latino Threat Narrative, cultural humility, advocacy, ethnic enclaves, and culturally responsive interventions. Pays special attention to the consequences of inequities in shaping community wellbeing. Same as ETHN 262.

title: INTRO TO ADDICTION STUDIES:ADDICTION AND THE COMMUNITY
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Explores historical, psychological, and sociological perspectives on the use, abuse, and social control of psychoactive drugs. Presents in depth analysis of the theoretical models of the biopsychosocial nature of addiction, the dynamics of addiction, the impact of addiction on children, families and society with emphasis on special populations, contemporary treatment and prevention approaches, and the addiction counseling profession.

title: GROUP PROCESS AND PRACTICE, LAWS AND ETHICS
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Presents group dynamics, theoretical modalities and practical skills involved in facilitating mental/ behavioral wellness counseling support groups across diverse population and ages. Explores the developmental stages of groups and practices that support group cohesion, self-reflection, and selfefficacy. Essential laws and the code of ethics associated with the counseling profession are also examined.

title: FAMILIES AND ADDICTION
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Examines common patterns of family structure and functioning often correlated with substance abuse and addiction including the major types of family systems and dynamics. Reviews basic clinical practice including therapeutic approaches, skills, and techniques for effective intervention and treatment modalities for both individuals and the family system.

title: TREATMENT AND CASE MANAGEMENT
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours/ 0.00 activity hours)
description: Presents theories, skills, techniques, and legal and ethical practices fundamental to client treatment and case management. Includes guidelines for developing assessments, diagnoses, and the implementation of treatment plans. Emphasizes working with chemically dependent individuals, survivors of intimate partner abuse, the homeless population, and individuals who are mentally impaired.

title: COUNSELING SKILLS, LAWS AND ETHICS
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours/ 0.00 activity hours)
description: Presents basic counseling skills and competencies for providing individual mental/behavioral health support, emphasizing person-centered and multicultural orientated practices. Related professional laws and ethical standards are examined.

title: HUMAN SERVICES SEMINAR
hours: 2 hours per week: (2.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours/ 0.00 activity hours)
description: 289D Prepares students to be successful in the concurrently enrolled fieldwork course, facilitating gainful employment in the human services and social work fields. Provides experiential practice and guidance for professional development through skill-building exercises, discussions and performance exams.

title: FIELDWORK: ADDICTION STUDIES
hours: 15 hours per week: (0.00 lecture hours/15.00 lab hours/0.00 activity hours)
description: Facilitates the application, within a supervised and approved substance abuse agency or institution, of students' previously gained knowledge and skills. Develops entry-level professional engagement that prepares students for employment in the field of substance abuse recovery and treatment.

title: FIELDWORK: SOCIAL WORK /HUMAN SERVICES
hours: 6 hours per week: (0.00 lecture hours/6.00 lab hours)
description: Facilitates a supervised field experience in the social work and human services profession, deepening application of previously gained knowledge and skills learned within the classroom environment. Provides students with an opportunity to further professional training in preparation for gaining employment.

title: FIELDWORK: ENTRY-LEVEL MENTAL WELLNESS COUNSELING
hours: 3 hours per week: (0.00 lecture hours/3.00 lab hours/ 0.00 activity hours)
description: Prepares students to apply knowledge and skills in the field of mental wellness support counseling in a supervised field setting (a community organization, agency, or institution), servicing youth or adults in emotional distress. Enhances and develops skills for employment within the profession.

title: BASIC UAV OPERATOR
hours: 5 hours per week: (2.00 lecture hours/3.00 lab hours)
description: Prepares students to meet the Federal Aviation Administration requirements for certification to operate Unmanned Aircraft Vehicles under 55 pounds for commercial operations pursuant to 14 CFR 107. Emphasizes the safe, legal, and ethical aspects of UAV operations in civil, public, and commercial settings. Includes special emphasis on capabilities and limitations of optical payloads and sensors, flight operation planning, and safety. Prepares students to safely operate UAV through all phases of flight to National Institute of Standards and Technology Level 2 Open Area Maneuvering remote pilot proficiency standards.

title: INTRODUCTION TO ANIMAL SCIENCE
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours/ 0.00 activity hours)
description: Provides students with an introduction to a scientific approach to the livestock industry, encompassing aspects of animal anatomy, physiology, nutrition, genetics and epidemiology. Emphasizes the origin, characteristics, adaptations, and contributions of livestock to the modern agriculture industry. Field trips may be required.

title: LIVESTOCK FEEDING ANDNUTRITION
hours: 5 hours per week: (2.00 lecture hours/3.00 lab hours)
description: Introduces the student to the science of animal nutrition. Covers the fundamentals of digestion and absorption in both ruminants and non-ruminants. Emphasizes the nutritive value of feedstuffs as they relate to the formulation of livestock rations. Laboratory required. Field trips may be required.

title: SMALL RUMINANT SCIENCE
hours: 5 hours per week: (2.00 lecture hours/3.00 lab hours)
description: Provides students with a detailed overview of the sheep and goat industries; management of commercial, purebred, and small farm flocks; selecting, feeding, breeding and basic care of small ruminants plus marketing of sheep, goats, and their products. Laboratory required. Field trips may be required.

title: EQUINE SCIENCE
hours: 5 hours per week: (2.00 lecture hours/3.00 lab hours)
description: Provides students with a detailed overview of the equine industry, encompassing the evolution and role of the equine species throughout history, breed selection and development, nutrition, disease, preventative health, reproductive management, basic horsemanship, and stabling alternatives. Laboratory required. Field trips may be required.

title: INTRODUCTION TO AGRICULTURAL STUDIES AND CAREERS
hours: 1 hours per week: (1.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours/ 0.00 activity hours)
description: Provides guidance for the educational pathways leading to degrees and certificates in agriculture. Emphasizes the exploration of agriculture careers and employment opportunities. Explores the skills necessary for success in obtaining, maintaining, and advancing in agriculture careers. Discusses current issues that affect agriculture.

title: AGRICULTURE ECONOMICS
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours/ 0.00 activity hours)
prereqs: Elementary Algebra or eligibility for transfer level math using the current college process Advisories: Intermediate Algebra or eligibility for transfer level math using the current college process.
description: Presents introductory concepts pertaining to agriculture and farming in the economic system. Topics include basic economic concepts, problems of agriculture, pricing and marketing problems, factors of production, and state and federal farm programs affecting the farmer's economic position.

title: INTRODUCTION TO AGRICULTURAL BUSINESS
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Provides a basic understanding of the business and economics of the agricultural industry; an introduction to the economic aspects of agriculture and their implications to the agricultural producer, consumer and the food system; management principles encountered in the day to day operation of an agricultural enterprise as they relate to the decision making process.

title: AGRICULTURAL SALES AND COMMUNICATION
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Examines principles and practices of the selling process including selling strategies and approaches, buyer behavior, prospecting, territory management, and customer service. Self- management, communication, leadership, teamwork and interpersonal skills necessary in developing managerial abilities within the agribusiness sector will be explored. Students will gain experience through role-play, formal sales presentations, and job shadowing. The course content is organized to give students an in-depth understanding of the factors and influences that affect the agribusiness industry on a day-to-day basis. Application of these concepts and methods will occur through hands-on projects developing solutions for agriculture business.

title: FARM MANAGEMENT
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Presents concepts related to the organization and operation of farm and ranch businesses. Topics include identification of factors affecting profitability, evaluation of the business for increased efficiency and profit and the application of budgeting to laboratory farm and independent analysis of a farm.

title: SUPERVISION AND MANAGEMENTIN AGRICULTURE
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours/ 0.00 activity hours)
description: Introduces students to the knowledge and skills relevant to the supervisor in agricultural business. Includes the regulatory requirements relevant to labor management in agriculture and effective communication with native and non-native English speakers. Includes case studies on labor management, human relations, public relations, production control techniques and job analysis.

title: INTRODUCTION TO AGRICULTURAL COMPUTER APPLICATIONS
hours: 4 hours per week: (4.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Introduces the student to computer use in the workplace with an emphasis on agribusiness situations. Computer applications including word processing, spreadsheets, databases and presentation software will be covered. Also included will be a working knowledge of computer terminology; relationship between hardware and software; computer operating systems and World Wide Web. The course also covers the ethical issues surrounding technology in an agribusiness setting. Credit for one course allowed between CIS 210 and AGB 210.

title: WORK EXPERIENCE IN AGRICULTURE BUSINESS
hours: 1.5 to 12 hours per week: (0.00 - 0.00 lecture hours/ 0.00 - 0.00 lab hours/1.50 - 12.00 work experience hours)
description: Provides opportunities for students in Ag Business to connect academic curricula to experiential learning in the workplace as an internship, Service Learning placement or general employment. Allows students to develop and work on learning objectives in workplace competencies and technical skills relevant for their course of study and career pathway. Students must work 54 hours for each unit of credit earned, in half-unit increments (27 hours), up to a maximum of 4 units. Employment can be paid or unpaid. Repeatable: 3 Times

title: FARM POWER, MACHINERY, AND SAFETY
hours: 6 hours per week: (2.00 lecture hours/4.00 lab hours/ 0.00 activity hours)
description: Introduces the safe and proper operation of wheel and track type tractors, their implements and their role in the agriculture industry. Also introduces the evaluation of agricultural machinery and tractor power performance and emphasis on management, selection, and efficient operation of agricultural machinery.

title: INTRODUCTION TO AGRICULTUREMECHANICS
hours: 6 hours per week: (2.00 lecture hours/4.00 lab hours)
description: Introduces basics in safety, tools, rope work, plumbing, concrete, blueprint reading, electrical, woodworking, metalworking and agriculture mechanics careers. Designed for students who seek to develop basic mechanical skills.

title: AGRICULTURAL SAFETY
hours: 2 hours per week: (2.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Involves safety practices and principles related to accident causation and prevention with tractors, machinery, livestock and environmental disposal and safe practice.

title: AGRICULTURE INDUSTRIAL POWER
hours: 6 hours per week: (2.00 lecture hours/4.00 lab hours)
description: Explores the basic operation and repair of modern diesel, natural gas, biofuel, and co-gen engines. Principles and theories are studied by running, testing, diagnosing, disassembling and reassembling components, systems, and engines. Additional emphasis will be placed on current California State Air Quality Control Standards.

title: SMALL GAS ENGINES
hours: 5 hours per week: (2.00 lecture hours/3.00 lab hours)
description: Introduces the operation, construction, maintenance, repair, and adjustments of two-cycle and four-cycle engines. Designed for persons without prior experience in small engines. Theory and practical work, including safety, customer service, and the care and use of specialized tools used in small engine repair and maintenance will be covered. Examples of the types of engines to be used will include lawn mower, power saw, pump, conveyor, self-propelled small carts, and any other small engines. Laboratory required.

title: WORK EXPERIENCE IN AGRICULTURE MECHANICS
hours: 1.5 to 12 hours per week: (0.00 - 0.00 lecture hours/ 0.00 - 0.00 lab hours/1.50 - 12.00 work experience hours)
description: Provides opportunities for students in Agriculture Mechanics to connect academic curricula to experiential learning in the workplace as an internship, Service Learning placement or general employment. Allows students to develop and work on learning objectives in workplace competencies and technical skills relevant for their course of study and career pathway. Students must work 54 hours for each unit of credit earned, in half-unit increments (27 hours), up to a maximum of 4 units. Employment can be paid or unpaid. Repeatable: 3 Times

title: PRINCIPLES OF IRRIGATION
hours: 6 hours per week: (2.00 lecture hours/4.00 lab hours/ 0.00 activity hours)
description: Introduces the fundamentals of basic irrigation systems including: flood, sprinkler, micro, subirrigation and their variations. Examine water use, quality, management and distribution systems in California and uncover the importance of water in the California Agriculture Industry.

title: INTRODUCTION TO SOIL SCIENCE
hours: 6 hours per week: (2.00 lecture hours/4.00 lab hours/ 0.00 activity hours)
description: Introduces the study of soil physical, chemical and biological properties. Soil classification, derivation, use, function and management including erosion, moisture retention, structure, cultivation, organic matter and microbiology. Laboratory topics include soil type, classification, soil reaction, soil fertility and physical properties of soil.

title: INTRODUCTION TO PLANT SCIENCE
hours: 6 hours per week: (2.00 lecture hours/4.00 lab hours/ 0.00 activity hours)
description: Provides students with a working knowledge of the fundamental structures and processes of plants. Principles to be applied cover plant structures, physiology, heredity, environmental relationship to growth, adaptation, and management of crops. Scientific research, exploration of plant growth, and identification of economical crops will be included.

title: PLANT PROPAGATION AND PRODUCTION
hours: 6 hours per week: (2.00 lecture hours/4.00 lab hours/ 0.00 activity hours)
description: Examines plant propagation and production with emphasis on nursery operations including sexual and asexual reproduction, planting, transplanting, fertilizing, plant pest and disease control; structures and site layout; preparation and use of propagating and planting mediums; use and maintenance of common tools and equipment; regulations pertaining to plant production. Laboratory required.

title: PLANT IDENTIFICATION AND USAGE I
hours: 6 hours per week: (2.00 lecture hours/4.00 lab hours/ 0.00 activity hours)
description: Covers the identification, growth habits, culture and ornamental use of landscape and indoor plants adapted to climates of California. Topics include botanical nomenclature, plant hardiness and growth zones, growth habits, plant structural characteristics and soil nutritional requirements. Landscape uses are stressed along with cultural practices. Plants covered are those best observed and identified in the Spring season of the year.

title: INTRODUCTION TO SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours/ 0.00 activity hours)
description: Introduces the history, definitions, concepts, principles and practices of sustainable agricultural systems. Includes an examination of case studies to connect sustainable agriculture principles to actual farming practices.

title: INTRODUCTION TO VITICULTURE
hours: 6 hours per week: (2.00 lecture hours/4.00 lab hours/ 0.00 activity hours)
description: Introduces viticulture including grape growing, history, distribution, biology, anatomy, propagation, cultivated varieties, rootstocks, climate, vineyard practices, common diseases and pests.

title: VITICULTURE PRACTICES
hours: 6 hours per week: (2.00 lecture hours/4.00 lab hours/ 0.00 activity hours)
description: Develops knowledge of sustainable vineyard practices including pruning, vine training, fertilizers, irrigation, crop and canopy management. Includes the study of weed control, harvest operations and pest and disease management.

title: WORK EXPERIENCE IN AGRICULTURE PLANT SCIENCE
hours: 1.5 to 12 hours per week: (0.00 - 0.00 lecture hours/ 0.00 - 0.00 lab hours/1.50 - 12.00 work experience hours)
description: Provides opportunities for students in Agriculture Plant Science to connect academic curricula to experiential learning in the workplace as an internship, Service Learning placement or general employment. Allows students to develop and work on learning objectives in workplace competencies and technical skills relevant for their course of study and career pathway. Students must work 54 hours for each unit of credit earned, in half-unit increments (27 hours), up to a maximum of 4 units. Employment can be paid or unpaid. Repeatable: 3 Times

hours: 1.5 to 6 hours per week: (0.00 - 0.00 lecture hours/ 1.50 - 6.00 lab hours)
prereqs: The student must have completed preparatory course work in the field in which the study is to be undertaken.
description: Provides an opportunity for an in-depth study or practicum experience by an individual student in a selected topic of American Sign Language under the direction of an instructor. ASL 201 AMERICAN SIGN LANGUAGE I 5.00 5 hours per week: (5.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours) Credit - Degree Applicable Introduces a functional-notional approach to the acquisition of American Sign Language (ASL) - a visual/gestural language - through the development of visual receptive and expressive skills required for vocabulary development, grammar, non-manual behaviors, and fingerspelling. Creates awareness of Deaf Culture by reviewing the history of ASL, dynamics of the Deaf community and cultural customs of communication.

title: AMERICAN SIGN LANGUAGE II
hours: 5 hours per week: (5.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Presents a continuation of ASL 201 through vocabulary development, grammar, non-manual behaviors and fingerspelling incorporating Deaf culture throughout. Heightens sensitivity to Deaf culture, including its history, values, traditions and communication customs.

title: PHYSICAL ANTHROPOLOGY
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Presents an introduction to the science of physical anthropology. Topics include: the fields of anthropology, the scientific method, evolutionary theory, genetics and inheritance, human variation, biology and behavior of living primates, and the fossil evidence of human evolution

title: PHYSICAL ANTHROPOLOGY LABORATORY
hours: 3 hours per week: (0.00 lecture hours/3.00 lab hours)
description: Utilizes the hands-on laboratory approach in studying primatology, osteology, dentition, genetics and human variation. Both fossil and contemporary will be studied.

title: ARCHAEOLOGY
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Presents an introduction to archaeological theory and concepts, as well as an overview of both New and Old World archaeology.

title: CULTURAL ANTHROPOLOGY
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Presents an anthropological study of culture. Cultural anthropologists study and compare human cultures throughout time. Students are introduced to how anthropologists do their work, utilize research ethics and study humans around the globe.

title: CALIFORNIA INDIANS
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours/ 0.00 activity hours)
description: Presents a history of the California Indians, including their prehistory, the Indians at the time of European contact, the Spanish period, the early Anglo-American period, and the Indians today.

title: NORTH AMERICAN INDIANS
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours/ 0.00 activity hours)
description: Studies the North American Indians, including their lifestyle at the time of contact, their reactions to European contact, and the Indians at present.

title: CONTEMPORARY CULTURES OF THE WORLD
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Studies the ways of life of people in different regions of the world, including Latin America, Middle East, East Asia, and Africa. Beliefs, values, and other social characteristics such as family, economics, and religion will be studied.

title: INDEPENDENT STUDIES: ANTHROPOLOGY
hours: 1.5 to 6 hours per week: (0.00 - 0.00 lecture hours/ 1.50 - 6.00 lab hours)
prereqs: The student must have completed preparatory course work in the field in which the study is to be undertaken
description: Provides an opportunity for an in-depth study or a practicum experience by an individual student in a selected topic of anthropology under the direction of an instructor.

title: UNDERGRADUATE STEM SEMINAR
hours: 1 to 2 hours per week: (1.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/0.00 - 0.00 lab hours/0.00 - 0.00 activity hours)
description: Introduces students to a variety of STEM fields (science, technology, engineering and mathematics) using a seminar format. Explores a broad range of academic and career opportunities in STEM. Emphasizes professional and personal skills for success in STEM. Same as BIO 295, ENGR 295, MATH 295, PSCI 295.

title: ARCHITECTURAL PORTFOLIO DESIGN WORKSHOP
hours: 1.1 hours per week: (0.22 lecture hours/0.88 lab hours)
description: Presents principles, concepts, methods, and skills pertaining to the design and preparation of architectural portfolios and presentations, with particular emphasis on using Adobe InDesign software for page layout and document production.

title: ARCHITECTURE SPECIAL TOPIC
hours: 0.5 to 4 hours per week: (0.50 - 4.00 lecture hours/ 0.00 - 0.00 lab hours)
description: Examines a special topic in the field of study related to the discipline offering this course.

title: ARCHITECTURAL MODEL MAKING
hours: 4 hours per week: (1.00 lecture hours/3.00 lab hours)
advisories: Completion of or concurrent enrollment in ARCH 222, ARCH 242, or high school drafting.
description: Introduces basic concepts and creation of 3D scaled material architectural models for visual representation and communication of architectural design.

title: HISTORY OF WORLD ## ARCHITECTURE I
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours/ 0.00 activity hours)
description: Surveys architecture and urbanism in the ancient world, from prehistory through the 16th century. Addresses the social, cultural and physical conditions that influenced the built environment of the Mediterranean basin, plus Europe, Asia, Africa, and Pre-Columbian America.

title: HISTORY OF WORLD ## ARCHITECTURE II
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours/ 0.00 activity hours)
description: Surveys architecture and urbanism from the beginning of the 17th century to the present. Addresses the social, cultural and physical conditions that influenced the built environment of Europe, Asia, Africa, and the Americas.

title: DESIGN AND VISUAL ## COMMUNICATION I
hours: 8 hours per week: (2.00 lecture hours/6.00 lab hours)
description: Presents principles, concepts, methods and skills pertaining to freehand and drafted drawings employing orthographic, axonometric, oblique and lineal perspective drawing systems to represent ideas, objects and environments. Includes principles and concepts of two- and three-dimensional visual design. Covers basic color theory principles, concepts and application; basic physical model building concepts and skills; shadow casting principles, conventions and techniques for orthographic, axonometric, oblique and perspective drawing systems.

title: DESIGN AND VISUAL ## COMMUNICATION II
hours: 8 hours per week: (2.00 lecture hours/6.00 lab hours)
description: Continuation and extension of the content and issues introduced in ARCH 211, plus the principles, concepts, methods and skills pertaining to the freehand, drafted and digital visualization and communication of quantitative and qualitative information to support analysis and conceptualization.

title: ARCHITECTURAL DESIGN & PRESENTATION COMPUTER GRAPHICS
hours: 5 hours per week: (2.00 lecture hours/3.00 lab hours)
description: Introduces computer design and presentation skills for architecture students including image editing, page layout, and 3D modeling.

title: INTRODUCTION TO ## ARCHITECTURAL PRACTICE
description: Introduces the concepts and methods associated with the use and application of construction systems, processes and materials. Emphasis is placed on the standards and conventions used to detail and document light framed construction.

title: ARCHITECTURAL ENVIRONMENT CONTROL SYSTEMS
hours: 5 hours per week: (2.00 lecture hours/3.00 lab hours)
advisories: Completion of or concurrent enrollment in ARCH 252.
description: Introduces the theory and application of climate, energy use and comfort as determinates of architectural form. Includes architectural methods of ventilating, cooling, heating, and lighting for envelope-load dominated buildings. Acceptable for credit, CSU, (credit based on portfolio review).

title: INDEPENDENT STUDIES: ARCHITECTURE
hours: 1.5 to 6 hours per week: (0.00 - 0.00 lecture hours/ 1.50 - 6.00 lab hours)
prereqs: The student must have completed preparatory course work in the field in which the study is to be undertaken
description: Provides an opportunity for an in-depth study or practicum experience by an individual student in a selected topic of architecture under direction of an instructor.

title: ARCHITECTURAL DESIGN FUNDAMENTALS I
hours: 9 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/6.00 lab hours)
description: Presents theories, principles, methods and means of creative problem solving, two- and threedimensional visual organizations to communicate concepts and meanings, basic verbal and visual communication skills, analysis of the built environment with emphasis on the creation and interrelationship of architectural form, function and light.

title: ARCHITECTURAL DESIGN FUNDAMENTALS II
hours: 9 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/6.00 lab hours/ 0.00 activity hours)
description: Continuation of theories, principles, methods and means of creative problem solving, two- and threedimensional visual organizations to communicate concepts and meanings, basic verbal and visual communication skills, analysis of the built environment with emphasis on the creation and interrelationship of architectural form, function, structure and context.

title: WORK EXPERIENCE IN ARCHITECTURE
hours: 1.5 to 12 hours per week: (0.00 - 0.00 lecture hours/ 0.00 - 0.00 lab hours/1.50 - 12.00 work experience hours)
description: Provides opportunities for students in Architecture to connect academic curricula to experiential learning in the workplace as an internship, Service Learning placement or general employment. Allows students to develop and work on learning objectives in workplace competencies and technical skills relevant for their course of study and career pathway. Students must work 54 hours for each unit of credit earned, in half-unit increments (27 hours), up to a maximum of 4 units. Employment can be paid or unpaid. Repeatable: 3 Times

title: ART SPECIAL TOPIC
hours: 0.5 to 4 hours per week: (0.50 - 4.00 lecture hours/ 0.00 - 0.00 lab hours)
description: Examines a special topic in the field of study related to the discipline offering this course.

title: ART OF AFRICA, OCEANIA, AND INDIGENOUS NORTH AMERICA
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours/ 0.00 activity hours)
description: Provides an overview of visual culture, including art and architecture, within select regions in sub- Saharan Africa, Oceania, and indigenous North America.

title: FUNDAMENTALS OF 2-D DESIGN
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 - 4.00 lab hours)
description: Introduces the design elements and principles common to all visual art forms including line, shape, value, texture, color, and space. Develops visual vocabulary for artistic expression through lecture presentations, creative problem solving, and studio projects.

title: DRAWING I
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 - 4.00 lab hours)
description: Introduces the history, theory, and practice of drawing as visual communication for both non-art and art majors. Explores principles, elements, and practices of drawing, employing a wide range of subject matter and drawing media. Presents drawing as a basic expression of visual thinking. Balances historical study and practice, combining practicality and aesthetic sense in an alternating sequence of observation and response. Examines concepts, techniques and conventions in contemporary and historical cultural contexts.

title: DRAWING II
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 - 4.00 lab hours)
description: Explores artistic concepts, styles, and creative expression related to intermediate-level drawing. Focuses on complex subject matter and concepts using a variety of drawing mediums, techniques, and methodologies. Students will incorporate personal approaches to content and materials in drawing projects covering both historical and contemporary methods.

title: FIGURE DRAWING I
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 - 4.00 lab hours)
description: Introduces drawing the human figure from observation of live models. Presents a wide variety of drawing media and techniques. Includes an introduction to human anatomy, the historical and contemporary roles of figure drawing in the visual arts, and expressive, interpretive approaches to drawing the figure.

title: FIGURE DRAWING II
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 - 4.00 lab hours)
description: Continues ART 223 with an emphasis on personal interpretation and the development of content. Focuses on the figure in context and in finished compositions.

title: COLOR
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 - 4.00 lab hours/0.00 - 0.00 activity hours)
description: Presents the physical nature of color and the theory of color. Explores primary systems, color properties, interaction, strategies and expressive qualities of color. Investigates the physiological, psychological, symbolic, and cultural aspects of color.

title: PAINTING I
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 - 4.00 lab hours/0.00 - 0.00 activity hours/0.00 - 0.00 work experience hours)
description: Introduces oil and acrylic painting techniques, methods, materials and concepts with a focus on contemporary practices. Emphasizes creative selfexpression, the elements and principles of design, and an examination of historical context.

title: PAINTING II
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 - 4.00 lab hours/0.00 - 0.00 activity hours)
description: Presents a continuation of ART 230A with a focus on contemporary issues in painting. Emphasizes composition and content.

title: PAINTING III
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 - 4.00 lab hours/0.00 - 0.00 activity hours)
description: Offers expanded instruction in intermediate level studio practices developed in Art 230B. Emphasizes exploration of historical and contemporary issues and trends in painting.

title: WATERCOLOR I
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 - 4.00 lab hours)
description: Introduces basic watercolor techniques, methods, and materials. Explores historical and cultural context as well as the creative use of aqueous media in painting on paper.

title: WATERCOLOR II
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 - 4.00 lab hours)
description: Continues ART 232 with an emphasis on problemsolving, composition, historical and cultural context, and the development of personal style.

title: FIGURE PAINTING
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 - 4.00 lab hours)
description: Introduces the fundamentals of painting from the human figure, the creative use of various painting media, and the figure in context.

title: PRINTMAKING I
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 - 4.00 lab hours)
description: Introduces instruction and studio practice in a variety of traditional printmaking techniques such as relief, intaglio, and screen-printing, as well as the designing of images appropriate to these techniques. Emphasizes contemporary art issues related to printmaking and the history of printmaking.

title: PRINTMAKING II
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 - 4.00 lab hours)
description: Offers further instruction in studio practices developed in Art 240A. Presents intermediate printmaking techniques in relief, intaglio, and screen-printing, as well as projects combining print processes. Emphasizes exploration of personal voice and contemporary cultural issues.

title: PRINTMAKING III
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 - 4.00 lab hours/0.00 - 0.00 activity hours/0.00 - 0.00 work experience hours)
description: Expands instruction in studio practices developed in Art 240B. Presents advanced-intermediate printmaking techniques in relief, intaglio, and screen-printing, as well as projects combining print processes. Emphasizes the creation of a body of artwork for portfolio presentation.

title: ETCHING I
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 - 4.00 lab hours)
description: Offers instruction and studio practice in beginning etching and drypoint printmaking techniques as well as the designing of images appropriate to these techniques.

title: ETCHING II
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 - 4.00 lab hours)
description: Offers instruction and studio practice in intermediate etching techniques as well as the designing of images appropriate to these techniques. Emphasizes contemporary art issues related to etching.

title: ETCHING III
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 - 4.00 lab hours)
description: Offers instruction and studio practice in expanded intermediate etching techniques including multiple plate printing and collagraph. Emphasizes contemporary art issues related to etching.

title: BOOK ARTS I
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 - 4.00 lab hours)
description: Presents an investigation of the book form as a vehicle of creative expression. Explores the book structure through the history, concepts and the creative application of this unique art object, in which the content is not limited to words alone.

title: BOOK ARTS II
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 - 4.00 lab hours/0.00 - 0.00 activity hours)
description: Continues instruction in studio practices developed in Art 243A. Presents intermediate level book binding and printing techniques in the conceptualization and construction of unique Artists’ Books. Emphasizes exploration of historical and contemporary issues and trends in text-based arts and artists' books.

title: PHOTOGRAPHY I
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 - 4.00 lab hours)
description: Introduces the processes, principles, and tools of black and white photography. Topics include the development of technical and aesthetic skills, the elements of design and composition, camera technology, materials, and equipment, within an historical and contemporary context. A 35mm film camera is required for class.

title: PHOTOGRAPHY II
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 - 4.00 lab hours)
description: Continues the study of photography as a fine art. Presents intermediate-level concepts, processes, principles, and tools of black and white photography. Emphasizes the development of photographic work as a means of personal expression through content, the elements of design and composition, and technique. Considers photography in a historical and contemporary context. Requires a 35mm film camera.

title: DIGITAL PHOTOGRAPHY I
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 - 4.00 lab hours)
description: Introduces the processes, principles, and tools of digital photography. Includes the development of technical and aesthetic skills, the elements of design and composition, camera technology, materials and equipment, within an historical and contemporary context.

title: DIGITAL PHOTOGRAPHY II
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 - 4.00 lab hours)
description: Continues the study of digital photography as a fine art. Presents intermediate level concepts, processes, principles, and tools of digital photography. Emphasizes the development of image-based works as a means of personal expression through content, the elements and principles of design and composition, and applicable digital imaging techniques. Considers photography in a historical and contemporary context.

title: WORK EXPERIENCE IN ART
hours: 1.5 to 12 hours per week: (0.00 - 0.00 lecture hours/ 0.00 - 0.00 lab hours/1.50 - 12.00 work experience hours)
description: Provides opportunities for students in Art to connect academic curricula to experiential learning in the workplace as an internship, Service Learning placement or general employment. Allows students to develop and work on learning objectives in workplace competencies and technical skills relevant for their course of study and career pathway. Students must work 54 hours for each unit of credit earned, in half-unit increments (27 hours), up to a maximum of 4 units. Employment can be paid or unpaid. Repeatable: 3 Times

title: ALTERNATIVE PHOTOGRAPHICPROCESSES
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 - 4.00 lab hours)
description: Explores creative photographic techniques emphasizing experimental manipulation of the photographic image. Introduces silver and nonsilver alternative photographic techniques including multiple image usage, high contrast materials, toning, image transfer, and digital negative with emphasis on personal expression, content, and development of style.

title: PHOTOGRAPHIC LIGHTING
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 \- 4.00 lab hours)
description: Explores various photographic lighting techniques emphasizing artificial sources. Introduces the student to modifying available light, tungsten light and strobe light on location and in the studio environment.

title: DIGITAL ART
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 - 4.00 lab hours/0.00 - 0.00 activity hours/0.00 - 0.00 work experience hours)
description: Introduces digital art production and marketing. Explores traditional art principles and cutting-edge technologies, including digital photo, vector, video, 3D, AR, and AI applications in a fine arts context.

title: FOUNDATION OF DIGITAL GRAPHIC ART
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 - 4.00 lab hours)
description: Presents primary instruction in digital vector graphic and illustration using Adobe Illustrator and other Adobe Creative Cloud software. Students will explore visual problem solving and utilize industry standard digital tools to create graphic works for artistic illustration, graphic design and user experience workflow.

title: FOUNDATION OF DIGITAL IMAGING ART
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 - 4.00 lab hours)
description: Presents primary instruction to enhance digital photographs and compose images using Adobe Photoshop and other Adobe Creative Cloud software. Students will use the latest Adobe Photoshop, Adobe Bridge and Adobe Camera Raw to explore visual problem solving and create images for photography, artistic digital image art, graphic design and user experience workflow.

title: INDESIGN LAYOUT DESIGN
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 - 4.00 lab hours)
description: Instructs designing print and digital layouts with Adobe InDesign and other industrial-standard software. Covers basic book, magazine, business, web, and UX design principles.

title: INTERACTION DESIGN I
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 \- 4.00 lab hours)
description: Provides a beginner-friendly introduction to interaction design, Web design, and user experience (UX) using Adobe Creative Cloud and other app design platforms. Emphasizes web and interactive design principles, including content structuring, efficient workflow, usability analysis, and testing techniques. Provides hands-on skills with modern design tools and explores responsive and dynamic design approaches. Introduces WordPress, web hosting, and FTP fundamentals.

title: MOTION GRAPHIC DESIGN
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 - 4.00 lab hours)
description: Takes students on a creative journey to learn the principles of motion graphic design. Explores topics of motion graphics, motion title design, AIinfluenced video editing, and After Effects visual effects. Introduces user interfaces to life with animation, the basics of 3D environment, and XR/ AR. Gives students the skills to unleash their creativity and shape the future of design with this immersive motion graphic design course.

title: GRAPHIC DESIGN
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 - 4.00 lab hours)
description: Explores visual design principles and processes in this career-focused, hands-on, project-based class. Introduces beginner-friendly design topics, including trending logo design, digital layout, graphics, illustrations, photography/images, web and UX design, animation, and video production. Emphasizes the incorporation symbols and typography into visual design and investigates the relationship between formal elements and symbolic content.

title: GRAPHIC DESIGN PORTFOLIO
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 - 4.00 lab hours)
description: Facilitates the development a professional design portfolio with new works created in class to support student success. Introduces current design strategies and techniques for career preparation, including AI. Emphasizes individualized design projects using digital layout, graphics, illustrations, photography, web and UX design, animation, and video.

title: TYPOGRAPHY
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 - 4.00 lab hours)
description: Introduces principles in the creative use of type in a digital environment. Emphasizes the use of typography in graphic design art. Includes topics such as the history of type, aesthetic qualities of letterforms, type classification, organization and hierarchy, grid systems and page layout.

title: FUNDAMENTALS OF 3-D DESIGN
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 - 4.00 lab hours)
description: Introduces the elements and principles of threedimensional design. Presents a variety of nonobjective studio projects using sculptural materials, tools, and methods. Includes the study of historical and contemporary art related to three-dimensional design and spatial composition.

title: SCULPTURE I
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 - 4.00 lab hours)
description: Introduces sculptural principles, techniques, and concepts utilizing a wide range of materials and a focus on contemporary practices. Emphasizes creative self-expression, the elements and principles of design, and an examination of historical context.

title: SCULPTURE II
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 - 4.00 lab hours)
description: Continues study of concepts and techniques of contemporary sculpture as introduced in ART 271. Presents intermediate-level assignments in fabrication and new genres with an emphasis on installation and site-specific public art. Addresses ongoing global, sociopolitical and cultural changes as well as incorporating new materials and technologies as tools for innovative art making.

title: SCULPTURE FOUNDRY: BRONZE CASTING I
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 - 4.00 lab hours)
description: Introduces basic theory and practice in cast bronze sculpture. Emphasizes creative self-expression using direct modeling of wax, basic mold making, and introduction to non-wax casting materials.

title: SCULPTURE FOUNDRY: BRONZE CASTING II
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 - 4.00 lab hours)
description: Continues instruction and practice in cast bronze sculpture. Emphasizes closed core casting, creative expression, and compositional organization of cast metal sculpture.

title: SCULPTURE FOUNDRY: BRONZE CASTING III
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 - 4.00 lab hours)
description: Continues instruction and practice in cast bronze sculpture and introduces aluminum casting. Emphasizes bronze repair using TIG welding, combining mixed media with cast metal, scale, and original compositional and formal themes.

title: CERAMICS I: INTRODUCTION TO CERAMICS
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 - 4.00 lab hours)
description: Introduces ceramics materials, concepts, and processes. Explores design principles, creative development, hand-building, throwing, glaze techniques, firing and ceramic terminology. Covers aesthetics and creative development of clay objects examining historical, contemporary, and personal modes of expression across cultures.

title: CERAMICS: WHEEL-THROWING I
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 - 4.00 lab hours)
description: Presents the practice of ceramic art with an emphasis on throwing on the potter's wheel including functional vessels and sculptural form derived from wheel-thrown objects and from combining wheel and handbuilt forms.

title: CERAMICS: WHEEL-THROWING II
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 - 4.00 lab hours)
description: Continues Art 281A with further development and refinement of throwing skills including functional vessels and sculptural forms derived from wheelthrown objects and from combining wheel and handbuilt forms. Includes development of surface, glazing and firing techniques at an intermediate level. Addresses aesthetics and creative development of clay objects examining historical, contemporary, and personal modes of expression.

title: CERAMICS II: HAND-BUILDING
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 - 4.00 lab hours)
description: Presents the practice of ceramic art with an emphasis on hand-building techniques. Includes functional vessels and sculptural forms and addresses traditional, historical, and contemporary issues. Guides the development of personal and artistic expression.

title: CERAMICS III: CERAMICS SCULPTURE
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 - 4.00 lab hours)
description: Presents a studio class dealing with issues and techniques of traditional and contemporary ceramic sculpture. Covers technical processes and materials relevant to ceramic sculpture. Guides the development of personal and artistic expression.

title: CERAMICS ALTERNATIVE MATERIALS AND PROCESSES
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 - 4.00 lab hours)
description: Presents instruction and gives experience in experimental applications of alternative firing techniques, processes, and material exploration of clay and ceramic media. Firings, processes, and materials will span temperatures and techniques including experimental applications in low fire, midrange and high fire temperatures. \- 4.00 lab hours) A body of artworks to include a minimum of twelve pieces which have been completed in college studio art courses. Introduces professional presentation techniques in Studio Art and Graphic Design. Includes the selection, photographing, and mounting of artwork for the production of a physical and a digital portfolio. Covers resume writing, artists statements, and letters of introduction. Examines career opportunities in various art-related fields and investigates four-year programs and requirements. Intended especially for the Studio Art or Graphic Design major near the completion of their studies at Cuesta College.

title: DESIGN FOR INNOVATION
hours: 2 hours per week: (2.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours/ 0.00 activity hours)
description: Develops creative problem-solving skills through innovation and human-centered design. Includes identifying community issues and problems; and sketching, creating, developing, testing, and prototyping potential solutions. Provides practice with hands-on exercises and design thinking activities for visual artists, designers, engineers, makers, entrepreneurs, marketers, and others. Same as BUS 296.

title: INDEPENDENT STUDIES: ART
hours: 1.5 to 6 hours per week: (0.00 - 0.00 lecture hours/ 1.50 - 6.00 lab hours)

description: Provides an opportunity for an in-depth study or a practicum experience by an individual student in a selected topic of Art under the direction of an instructor.

title: ART APPRECIATION
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Examines works of art through the study of terminology, themes, design principles, media and techniques, and provides a general introduction to the visual arts across time and diverse cultures through the use of various art historical methodologies.

title: INTRODUCTION TO MUSEUM PRACTICES
hours: 5 hours per week: (2.00 lecture hours/3.00 lab hours)
advisories: ENGL C1000 and ARTH C1100 or ARTH
description: C1200 or ARTH 205 or ARTH 207 or ARTH 208 or ARTH 210 or ARTH 211 Introduces the history, functions, and professional practices of art museums. Includes development of an art historical exhibition and accompanying texts. Introduces curatorial and art critical writing, including writing art reviews for publication.

title: SURVEY OF MODERN AND CONTEMPORARY ART HISTORY
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Presents an overview of the art movements, artists and issues of Modernism to Contemporary art. This includes art from the mid-nineteenth century, through the twentieth century and contemporary art. Incorporates the social, political, and aesthetic context of the time.

title: LATIN AMERICAN ART HISTORY I: ANCIENT
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Surveys the arts, architecture, and archaeology of ancient Mesoamerica and South America from 1200 BCE to the conquest/16th century.

title: SURVEY OF MEXICAN ART HISTORY
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Surveys the arts, architecture, and visual culture of Mexico from the colonial period/16th century to the present.

title: SURVEY OF ASIAN ART HISTORY
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Provides an overview of Asian art and architecture. Includes cultural and historical background of artistic traditions of India, Southeast Asia, China, Korea, and Japan from prehistoric to modern times.

title: SURVEY OF AFRICAN ART HISTORY
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours/ 0.00 activity hours)
description: Provides an overview of the arts and architecture of Africa. Examines social and historical contexts of artistic production.

title: ART GALLERY
hours: 5 to 6 hours per week: (2.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/3.00 - 4.00 lab hours)
description: Explores theoretical, technical, and aesthetic aspects of exhibiting works of art. Provides actual experience in operating an art gallery. Students will work with exhibiting artists, learn about contemporary issues in art, and the relationship between gallery, artist, and viewing public. Students assist in design, publicity, installation, and management of the Cuesta College Art Gallery.

title: SURVEY OF ART FROM PREHISTORY TO THE MEDIEVAL ERA
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: This course introduces students to visual art and architecture from prehistory to the medieval era with a focus on art from Europe, North Africa, and the near East. The course will further consider global interactions involving these regions.

title: SURVEY OF ART FROM THE RENAISSANCE TO CONTEMPORARY
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: This course provides an overview of art and architecture from the Renaissance to the contemporary period with a focus on art from Europe. The course will further consider global interactions involving this region.

title: ASTRONOMY
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
prereqs: Elementary algebra or eligibility for college-level math using the current college process. Advisories: Eligibility for ENGL C1000
description: Presents the astronomy of planets, satellites, asteroids, comets, meteors, the sun, stars, and galaxies.

title: ASTRONOMY LAB
hours: 3 hours per week: (0.00 lecture hours/3.00 lab hours)
prereqs: Elementary algebra or eligibility for college-level math using the current college process. Corequisites: ASTR 210
description: Presents the principles of measurement, data collection and analysis to the astronomical phenomena of celestial motions and characteristics of planets, stars, galaxies in the planning, execution, and presentation of research projects.

title: ASTRONOMY RESEARCH SEMINAR
hours: 2 hours per week: (0.67 lecture hours/1.33 lab hours)
description: Provides practical experience in one area of astronomical research, and an understanding of the nature of scientific research. Students plan a research project, make observations, analyze results, and write a paper for publication.

hours: 5 to 10 hours per week: (0.00 - 0.00 lecture hours/ 5.00 - 10.00 lab hours)
description: Presents the theory and practice of track and field athletics. Includes the rules and fundamentals of the track and field events and participation in intercollegiate track meets. Repeatable: 3 Times

description: Introduces strength and fitness building as well as the fundamentals and techniques of multiple track and field events in preparation for spring competition. Repeatable: 3 Times

title: OFF-SEASON TRAINING FOR FALL ATHLETES II

description: Provides fall sport off-season emphasis on aerobic and anaerobic conditioning, sport-specific techniques, sports-specific strength development, play strategies, and nutrition for the fall off-season athlete. Repeatable: 3 Times

description: Provides spring sport off-season emphasis aerobic and anaerobic conditioning, sports-specific techniques, sports-specific strength development, play strategies and nutrition for the spring offseason athlete. Repeatable: 3 Times

description: This course is designed to provide a physical conditioning program for the student interested in Fall Intercollegiate Athletics Programs. Repeatable: 3 Times

title: WOMEN'S INTERCOLLEGIATE WATER POLO
hours: 5 to 10 hours per week: (0.00 - 0.00 lecture hours/ 5.00 - 10.00 lab hours)
prereqs: Students must possess advanced intercollegiate athletics skills and knowledge to participate, which will be determined by the instructor.
description: Presents an opportunity for physically advanced students to further develop knowledge and skill in the sport of water polo. This offering is appropriate for students desiring the physical, mental and emotional challenges that are inherent in competition against students representing other colleges. Repeatable: 3 Times

title: MEN'S INTERCOLLEGIATE WATER POLO

title: NONCREDIT BASIC SKILLS BIOLOGY
