description: Provides an opportunity for an in-depth study or a practicum experience by an individual student in a selected topic of Oceanography under the direction of an instructor.

title: WORK EXPERIENCE IN OCEANOGRAPHY
hours: 1.5 to 12 hours per week: (0.00 - 0.00 lecture hours/ 0.00 - 0.00 lab hours/1.50 - 12.00 work experience hours)
description: Provides opportunities for students in Oceanography to connect academic curricula to experiential learning in the workplace as an internship, Service Learning placement or general employment. Allows students to develop and work on learning objectives in workplace competencies and technical skills relevant for their course of study and career pathway. Students must work 54 hours for each unit of credit earned, in half-unit increments (27 hours), up to a maximum of 4 units. Employment can be paid or unpaid.

title: CURRENT ETHICAL ISSUES FORPARALEGALS
hours: 1 hours per week: (1.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Examines current ethical issues for paralegals using case law and examples of lawyer and paralegal misconduct.

title: INDEPENDENT STUDIES: PARALEGAL
hours: 1.5 to 6 hours per week: (0.00 - 0.00 lecture hours/ 1.50 - 6.00 lab hours)
prereqs: The student must have completed preparatory course work in the field in which the study is to be undertaken.
description: Provides an opportunity for an in-depth study or a practicum experience by an individual student in a selected topic of Paralegal under the direction of an instructor.

title: INTRODUCTION TO PARALEGALSTUDIES
hours: 4 hours per week: (2.50 lecture hours/1.50 lab hours)
description: Introduces the professional responsibilities of the paralegal, including rules regarding ethical conduct and a basic overview of the legal system and research. Covers different law office management functions commonly performed by paralegals such as basic correspondence, billing and financial management, calendar and docket control management, file and record management, and library management.

title: PARALEGAL INTERNSHIP
hours: 8 hours per week: (0.50 lecture hours/7.50 lab hours)
description: Provides students an opportunity to experience the responsibilities of an employee in a legal setting related to their courses in paralegal studies.

title: CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LITIGATION
hours: 5 hours per week: (3.50 lecture hours/1.50 lab hours)
description: Introduces the principles and management of civil litigation in state and federal courts including pretrial, trial, and post trial practice and procedures. Covers pleadings, discovery, pretrial motions, trial preparation, trial motions, trial assistance, post trial motions, enforcement of judgments, and appeals. Procedures used in case settlement and in alternative dispute resolution such as mediation and arbitration will also be covered.

title: BUSINESS ORGANIZATIONS
description: Introduces the student to the substantive law and procedural aspects of business organizations, including sole proprietorships, partner ships, limited liability companies, and corporations. Includes a study of the relative advantages and disadvantages of the different business organizations as related to formation, management, liability, dissolution, regulation, and taxation. Also includes an overview of such related areas as agency law, employment law, and business ethics.

title: FAMILY LAW
hours: 4 hours per week: (2.50 lecture hours/1.50 lab hours)
description: Introduces the fundamental principles of California Family Law along with the terminology, procedures, and legal document and form preparation involved in family law matters. Topics include an overview of California law regarding marriage versus domestic partnerships, principles of community property law, marital and cohabitation agreements, legal separations, marital and domestic partnership dissolutions, annulments, spousal and domestic partner support, child custody and support, paternity, adoption, and domestic violence.

title: ESTATE PLANNING AND ADMINISTRATION
hours: 4 hours per week: (2.50 lecture hours/1.50 lab hours)
description: Introduces the fundamental principles of estate planning and administration along with the terminology, procedures, and legal document and form preparation involved in estate planning and administration matters. Topics cover aspects of estate planning including the preparation of wills, trusts, and related documents along with aspects of estate administration including probate proceedings and estate disposition outside of probate.

title: TECHNOLOGY IN THE LAW OFFICE
hours: 4 hours per week: (2.50 lecture hours/1.50 lab hours)
description: Introduces the student to the use of technology by paralegals in the law office. Includes an overview of technology in the law office and the ethical issues raised by the use of such technology. Covers computer applications in the law office including word processing and document assembly, spreadsheets, database management, law office management, case management and litigation support as well as electronic discovery. Also covers computer assisted legal research including CD-ROM and internet legal and factual research.

title: DEBT COLLECTION & ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Explains the procedures, forms, and strategies for enforcing and satisfying a monetary judgment. Covers state and federal laws relating to consumer and business debt collection. Includes secured vs. unsecured debt, judicial liens, writs of execution, levying on personal and real property, preparing wage garnishments, claiming exemptions, and ethical considerations relating to debt collection.

title: LEGAL RESEARCH AND WRITING
hours: 4 hours per week: (4.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Provides an introduction to the fundamental aspects of legal research by an in-depth analysis of case law, statutory law, and administrative law on both a federal and state level. Students will learn to locate authority relevant to selected legal issues. This skill is applied to writing clear and concise briefs, opinion letters, and memoranda, employing the IRAC (issue, rule, analysis, conclusion) legal analytical formula.

title: CAREER PLANNING: COMPREHENSIVE
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Introduces a decision-making process that will help students envision and plan for a future that is productive, achievable, and stimulating. The culmination of this process is the development of an online career and education 10-year plan that can be used for advisory and academic coaching purposes and updated as students grow, change, or face transitions. The personalized 10-year plan provides the focus and intrinsic motivation to succeed in college, at work, and in life.

title: INTRODUCTION TO THE BIBLE
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Introduces the literature of the Hebrew scriptures and the Christian New Testament through their history, literary conventions, authors, and sources.

title: INTRODUCTION TO PHILOSOPHY
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Introduces the ideas and methods of major philosophers through the critical reading of selections from primary texts. Emphasis will be placed on the philosophical subfields of metaphysics, epistemology, and ethics. May also include philosophical examination of topics in religion, science, language, art, or politics.

title: CRITICAL REASONING AND WRITING
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Develops and refines the critical thinking skills necessary to understand, evaluate, and produce arguments. Emphasizes the reasoning skills employed in writing effective academic essays.

title: WORLD RELIGIONS
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours/ 0.00 activity hours)
description: Presents the history, concepts, and cultures of the world's major religions. Emphasizes Judaism, Christianity, Islam, Hinduism, and Buddhism. Surveys Jainism, Confucianism, Taoism, Zoroastrianism, Shintoism, and Sikhism.

title: PHILOSOPHICAL CLASSICS IN THEORY OF REALITY AND OF KNOWLEDGE
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Presents an in-depth study of problems in the theory of reality and the theory of knowledge by means of a critical analysis of a selection of classics in philosophy.

title: PHILOSOPHICAL CLASSICS IN ETHICS AND SOCIAL PHILOSOPHY
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Studies problems in ethics and social philosophy by critically analyzing a selection of classic texts.

title: INDEPENDENT STUDIES:PHILOSOPHY
hours: 1.5 to 6 hours per week: (0.00 - 0.00 lecture hours/ 1.50 - 6.00 lab hours/0.00 - 0.00 activity hours)
prereqs: The student must have completed preparatory course work in the field in which the study is to be undertaken.
description: PHILOSOPHY 0.50 to 2.00 Provides an opportunity for in-depth study or a practicum experience by an individual student in a selected topic of philosophy under the direction of an instructor.

title: PHLEBOTOMY
hours: 3.6 hours per week: (1.44 lecture hours/2.16 lab hours)
prereqs: Student must be 18 years of age by the first class meeting. Proof of high school or equivalent education.
coreqs: PHLB 109B and Current Health Care Provider CPR
description: Prepares the student in essential blood specimen collecting skills to fulfill the State of California phlebotomy certificate requirements for a a Certified Phlebotomy Technician (CPT-1). Prepares students for employment in hospitals, independent labs, physician offices, or public health clinics. Hands-on externship experience is part of the training (via corequisite PHLB 109B). The Student is required to bring a valid CA driver's license or CA photo ID card to the first class meeting to show proof of age. The student must be 18 years of age by the first class meeting to be certified.

title: PHLEBOTOMY EXTERNSHIP
hours: 3 hours per week: (0.00 lecture hours/3.00 lab hours)
prereqs: Student must be 18 years of age by the first class meeting.
description: Provides students the opportunity to participate in an externship that allows application of knowledge and skills in an acute and/or ambulatory care laboratory setting. Helps students obtain the minimum requirements for obtaining a State of California CPT-1 Certificate.

title: ENERGY AND MATTER
hours: 6 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/3.00 lab hours/ 0.00 activity hours)
prereqs: Intermediate algebra or eligibility for college-level math using the current college process.
description: Investigates basic principles of physics and chemistry. This activity-based course provides an introduction to the basic concepts of physical science with emphasis on their practical importance and application in the real world. Designed for nonscience majors, concepts are introduced in lab through inquiry and further developed during discussion.

title: EARTH SCIENCE
hours: 6 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/3.00 lab hours/ 0.00 activity hours)
prereqs: Elementary algebra or eligibility for college-level math using the current college process.
description: Introduces the essentials of Earth Science including a laboratory component. Topics include the geosphere, atmosphere, hydrosphere, and solar system. This course focuses on the interactions between physical and chemical systems of the Earth such as the tectonic cycle, rock cycle, hydrologic cycle, weather and climate.

title: ENERGY, ELECTRICITY, AND THE ENVIRONMENT
hours: 1 hours per week: (0.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours/ 1.00 activity hours/0.00 work experience hours)
description: Introduces students to basic theoretical and practical concepts in electrical energy production, measurements, usage, and storage. Provides opportunities to research and analyze potential environmental impacts related to the methods in which energy is produced.

title: PHYSICAL SCIENCE RESEARCH ASSISTANT
hours: 0.5 to 2 hours per week: (0.50 - 2.00 lecture hours/ 0.00 - 0.00 lab hours/0.00 - 0.00 activity hours)
limitation: Enrollment requires panel review of student research goals involving two or more faculty
description: Applies principles and methods of research in any of the various disciplines encompassed by the physical sciences.

title: UNDERGRADUATE STEM SEMINAR
hours: 1 to 2 hours per week: (1.00 - 2.00 lecture hours/0.00 - 0.00 lab hours/0.00 - 0.00 activity hours)
description: Introduces students to a variety of STEM fields (science, technology, engineering and mathematics) using a seminar format. Explores a broad range of academic and career opportunities in STEM. Emphasizes professional and personal skills for success in STEM. Same as ANTH 295, BIO 295, ENGR 295, MATH 295.

title: PHYSICS SPECIAL TOPIC
hours: 0.5 to 4 hours per week: (0.50 - 4.00 lecture hours/ 0.00 - 0.00 lab hours/0.00 - 0.00 activity hours)
description: Examines a special topic in the field of study related to the discipline offering this course.

title: ADVANCED PROBLEM SOLVING FOR PHYS 208B
hours: 1 hours per week: (1.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Supplements PHYS 208B to further develop general physics skills and conceptual understanding. Provides the opportunity for additional assistance in developing and mastering problem-solving abilities.

title: GENERAL PHYSICS
hours: 6 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/3.00 lab hours)
transfer: CSU; UC C-ID:C-ID PHYS 105. PHYS 205A+205B = C-ID PHYS 100S
description: Presents the principles of statics and dynamics of particles and rigid bodies, harmonic motion, fluid mechanics, heat, thermodynamics, wave motion and sound using trigonometry.

title: GENERAL PHYSICS
hours: 6 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/3.00 lab hours)
transfer: CSU; UC C-ID:C-ID PHYS 110. PHYS 205A+205B = C-ID PHYS 100S
description: Presents the principles of geometric optics, physical optics, static and dynamic electricity and magnetism, introductory DC and AC circuit theory, modern physics topics (relativity, particles and waves, atomic structure, radioactivity and nuclear reactions) using trigonometry.

title: PRINCIPLES OF PHYSICS 1
hours: 7 hours per week: (4.00 lecture hours/3.00 lab hours)
transfer: CSU; UC C-ID:C-ID PHYS 205. PHYS 208A+208B+208C = C-ID PHYS 200S
description: Presents the principles of statics and dynamics of particles and rigid bodies, fluids, harmonic motion, heat and thermodynamics using calculus.

title: DIRECTED PROBLEM SOLVING METHODS FOR PHYS 208A
hours: 1 hours per week: (1.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Presents problem-solving and fundamenta reasoning skills needed for success in PHYS 208A, Principles of Physics I. This course is designed for students who are currently enrolled in PHYS 208A and seek to improve their problem solving skills and mastery of concepts presented in PHYS 208A. Topics include specific techniques for solving kinematics, force, energy, momentum, torque, thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, and simple harmonic motion problems, analysis of word problems, and the development of solution maps.

title: PRINCIPLES OF PHYSICS 2
hours: 7 hours per week: (4.00 lecture hours/3.00 lab hours)
transfer: C-ID:C-ID PHYS 210. PHYS 208A+208B+208C = PHYS 200S; CSU; UC
description: Presents the principles of wave motion, sound, geometric and physical optics, static and dynamic electricity and magnetism, D.C. and A.C. circuit theory and electromagnetic waves using calculus.

title: DIRECTED PROBLEM SOLVING METHODS FOR PHYS 208B
hours: 1 hours per week: (1.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Presents problem-solving and fundamental reasoning skills needed for success in PHYS 208B, Principles of Physics II. This course is designed for students who are currently enrolled in PHYS 208B and seek to improve their problem solving skills and mastery of concepts presented in PHYS 208B. Topics include specific techniques for modeling wave phenomena including sound, electromagnetic, and physical waves, and problem solving techniques utilized in charged systems subjected to magnetic fields.

title: MODERN PHYSICS
hours: 6 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/3.00 lab hours)
transfer: CSU; UC C-ID:C-ID PHYS 215. PHYS 208A+208B+208C = PHYS 200S
description: Presents the principles of relativity, waves and particles, Bohr theory, quantum mechanics and Schroedinger's equation, elementary atomic structure, nuclear structure and radioactivity using calculus and vector algebra.

title: WORK EXPERIENCE IN PHYSICS
hours: 1.5 to 12 hours per week: (0.00 - 0.00 lecture hours/ 0.00 - 0.00 lab hours/1.50 - 12.00 work experience hours)
description: Provides opportunities for students in Physics to connect academic curricula to experiential learning in the workplace as an internship, Service Learning placement or general employment. Allows students to develop and work on learning objectives in workplace competencies and technical skills relevant for their course of study and career pathway. Students must work 54 hours for each unit of credit earned, in half-unit increments (27 hours), up to a maximum of 4 units. Employment can be paid or unpaid. Repeatable: 3 Times

title: INTRODUCTION TO POLITICALSCIENCE
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Surveys the scope, methods and theories of political science with special emphasis on contemporary political issues and problems.

title: WORLD POLITICS
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Examines the nature of relations among states. Analyzes the basic forces affecting the formulation and implementation of foreign policy, and the dynamics of international politics. Emphasizes contemporary problems affecting the United States of America in relation to other nations of the world, and the consequences of those contemporary problems.

title: LAW AND POLITICS
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Introduces the political and constitutional context of major legal controversies, including but not limited to civil rights, civil liberties, presidential versus congressional power, and national versus state and local power.

title: COMPARATIVE GOVERNMENT
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Compares and analyzes different kinds of political systems; their history, political institutions, political processes, and the environments in which they occur and their consequences.

title: INTRODUCTION TO POLITICAL THEORY
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Surveys the diversity of ideas and concepts in political thought from the ancients to the present, from Plato to contemporary feminism.

title: INDEPENDENT STUDIES: POLITICALSCIENCE
hours: 1.5 to 6 hours per week: (0.00 - 0.00 lecture hours/ 1.50 - 6.00 lab hours/0.00 - 0.00 activity hours)
prereqs: The student must have completed preparatory course work in the field in which the study is to be undertaken.
description: Provides an opportunity for an in-depth study or practicum experience by an individual student in a selected topic of government under the direction of an instructor.

title: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT AND POLITICS
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: This course is an introduction to government and politics in the United States and California. Students examine the constitutions, structure, and operation of governing institutions, civil liberties and civil rights, political behaviors, political issues, and public policy using political science theory and methodology.

title: WELLNESS ARTS
hours: 3 hours per week: (1.50 lecture hours/1.50 lab hours)
description: Presents art as a tool for processing, expressing and managing mental health issues as they relate to succeeding in a college environment. Examines the fundamentals of mental wellness in the college setting and provides strategies for maintaining positive mental health. Designed for students who struggle with levels of anxiety, sadness, intrusive thoughts, and social phobia that may make attending and succeeding in college difficult.

title: SURVEY OF OFFICE PROCEDURES
hours: 2 hours per week: (0.50 lecture hours/1.50 lab hours/ 0.00 activity hours)
description: Presents a basic overview of professional office procedures in a hands-on learning environment, with an emphasis on the foundational knowledge and skills required for a basic entry level administrative office support position.

title: SURVEY OF RETAIL PROCEDURES
hours: 2 hours per week: (0.50 lecture hours/1.50 lab hours/ 0.00 activity hours) 0.5 hours per week: (0.50 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Presents a basic overview of professional retail procedures in a hands-on environment, with an emphasis on the foundational knowledge and skills required for basic entry-level retail positions. Provides students with an understanding of change and the influence it has on an organization and the individuals in that organization. Topics will include understanding organizational and individual change, theoretical models of change, and how to manage change.

title: TEAM BUILDING
hours: 0.5 hours per week: (0.50 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Provides the student with an understanding of how teams work together, common problems teams encounter and how to solve them. Students will learn to recognize various team player styles. Students will be introduced to team building in the workplace.

title: COMMUNICATING WITH PEOPLE
hours: 0.5 hours per week: (0.50 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Introduces the student to key elements in communication within business organizations. Topics will include verbal and nonverbal communication, listening skills and specific supervisory communication skills.

title: CONFLICT RESOLUTION
hours: 0.5 hours per week: (0.50 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Provides the student with an analysis of attitudes and behavior which create conflict between individuals and groups within an organization.

title: CUSTOMER SERVICE
hours: 0.5 hours per week: (0.50 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Provides the student with certain key skills and attitudes in order to effectively meet the needs of customers. The student will be introduced to the concept of internal and external customers, customer satisfaction and customer retention.

title: VALUES & ETHICS
hours: 0.5 hours per week: (0.50 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Acquaints the student with the importance of values and ethics in the workplace. The importance of values and ethics involved in carrying out one's duties will be emphasized.

title: ATTITUDE IN THE WORKPLACE
hours: 0.5 hours per week: (0.50 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Provides the student with certain key skills in the area of attitude so that they may effectively maintain a positive attitude at the workplace and at home. Concepts of how attitudes are communicated, the three types of attitudes and how to adjust one's attitude will be presented.

title: STRESS MANAGEMENT
hours: 0.5 hours per week: (0.50 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Acquaints the student with various skills the supervisor needs to help employees. Included is the recognition of stress and how to manage it.

title: DECISION MAKING & PROBLEM SOLVING
hours: 0.5 hours per week: (0.50 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Introduces the student to decision making and problem solving for the workplace.

title: TIME MANAGEMENT
hours: 0.5 hours per week: (0.50 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Introduces the student to time management principles and specific tools that assist in making maximum use of time.

title: RESEARCH METHODS FOR THE BEHAVIORAL AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
prereqs: PSYC C1000 STAT C1000 with a minimum grade of C or better or consent of instructor
description: Introduces research methods used in psychology and other social sciences. Topics include the logic and ethics of research; descriptive, correlational, and experimental methodology; instrumentation; strategies for searching research literature; basic statistical reasoning and methods; and the collection, analysis, interpretation, and reporting of research data.

title: INTRODUCTION TO BIOLOGICAL PSYCHOLOGY
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Presents an analysis of the biological bases of behavior and mental processes in terms of evolutionary, genetic, anatomical and physiological determinants. Examines heredity, development, cognitive processes, and the function of the nervous and endocrine systems.

title: INTRODUCTION TO ABNORMAL PSYCHOLOGY
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Introduces the scientific study of psychopathology and disorders of cognition and behavior, broadly defined. Students investigate abnormal behavior from a variety of perspectives including biological, psychological, and sociocultural approaches. An integrative survey of theory and research in psychopathology, and the intervention and prevention strategies for psychological disorders are also introduced.

title: INTRODUCTION TO SOCIAL PSYCHOLOGY
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: This course considers individual human behavior in relation to the social environment. The power of the situation, other individuals, and the social group will be examined. Emphasized topics include: aggression, prejudice and stereotypes, interpersonal attraction, attitudes and attitude change, conformity, group phenomena, gender roles, cultural norms, person perception, and social cognition.

title: PERSONALITY AND ADJUSTMENT
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Presents the scientific study of personality with an applied focus on how psychological science is used for personal growth and adjustment to life experiences. The course surveys different psychological perspectives and theoretical foundations of personality development and change, with consideration of the influence of personal relationships, culture, gender, ethnicity, historical context, and socio-economic status.

title: INDEPENDENT STUDIES:PSYCHOLOGY
hours: 1.5 to 6 hours per week: (0.00 - 0.00 lecture hours/ 1.50 - 6.00 lab hours/0.00 - 0.00 activity hours)
prereqs: The student must have completed preparatory course work in the field in which the study is to be undertaken.
description: Provides an opportunity for an in-depth study or a practicum experience by an individual student in a selected topic of psychology under the direction of an instructor.

title: INTRODUCTION TO PSYCHOLOGY
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: This course is an introduction to psychology, which is the study of the mind and behavior. Students focus on theories and concepts of biological, cognitive, developmental, environmental, social, and cultural influences; their applications; and their research foundations.

title: INTRODUCTION TO PSYCHIATRIC TECHNICIAN
hours: 6.7 hours per week: (6.67 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours/0.00 activity hours)
prereqs: Admission to the Psychiatric Technician Program
description: Introduces students to the psychiatric technician training program. Presents concepts necessary to practice safely and legally in a forensic mental institution. Emphasizes basic therapeutic communication, pharmacology, growth and development, developmental disabilities, behavior modification, nutrition, and nursing care, including application of basic skills to the care of patients with developmental disabilities

title: PSYCHIATRIC TECHNICIAN SPECIAL TOPIC
hours: 0.5 to 4 hours per week: (0.50 - 4.00 lecture hours/ 0.00 - 0.00 lab hours)
description: Examines a special topic in the field of study related to the discipline offering this course.

title: NURSING SCIENCE
hours: 27.2 hours per week: (10.56 lecture hours/16.67 lab hours)
description: Presents principles of Mental Health and Physical Health. Principles of Theory and Clinical Skills are applied in the care of patients in Long Term Care and Respite Day Care facilities. Students demonstrate competent skill performance in a simulated clinical setting. Principles of Nursing Process, Standard Nursing Care for a variety of common diseases and care of the elderly are also a focus.

title: CARE OF THE DEVELOPMENTALLY DISABLED
hours: 28.8 hours per week: (10.11 lecture hours/18.67 lab hours)
description: Introduces concepts of care for the developmentally disabled. Presents causes, prevention, and treatment of developmentally disabled disorders. Provides practice and the rise of rehabilitative methods, problem solving, and communication in providing client care.

title: PSYCHIATRIC NURSING
hours: 29 hours per week: (11.33 lecture hours/17.67 lab hours/0.00 activity hours)
description: Introduces psychological and mental health concepts. Presents causes, prevention, and treatment of mental, emotional and behavior disorders. Provides practice in interpersonal skills, self understanding, problem solving, communication, and the use of rehabilitative methods in providing client care.

title: PUBLIC HEALTH SCIENCE - ASPECTS OF DRUG USE
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Presents an in depth analysis of the major health problems associated with the use, misuse, and abuse of drugs including herbs/plants, performance enhancing, over-the-counter, prescription, controlled, and designer drugs. Emphasizes the metabolism of drugs, drug interactions, and addiction from various socio-cultural perspectives such as age, gender, and ethnicity.

title: INTRODUCTION TO PUBLIC HEALTH SCIENCE
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Provides an introduction to the discipline of Public Health. Students will gain an understanding of the basic concepts and terminologies of public health, and the history and accomplishments of public health officials and agencies. An overview of the functions of various public health professions and institutions, and an in-depth examination of the core public health disciplines is covered. Topics of the discipline include the epidemiology of infectious and chronic disease; prevention and control of diseases in the community including the analysis of the social determinants of health and strategies for eliminating disease, illness and health disparities among various populations; community organizing and health promotion programming; environmental health and safety; global health; and healthcare policy and management.

title: HEALTH AND SOCIAL JUSTICE
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
advisories: Eligibility for transfer-level English composition based on the current college process.
description: Provides an introduction to the health inequities in the United States that stem from unequal living conditions. Explores how education, socioeconomic status, racism, and gender shape health epidemics and policy development. Explores fundamental theories and demonstrate basic skills to advocate for health and social justice.

title: WORK EXPERIENCE IN PUBLIC HEALTH SCIENCE
hours: 1.5 to 12 hours per week: (0.00 - 0.00 lecture hours/ 0.00 - 0.00 lab hours/1.50 - 12.00 work experience hours)
description: Provides opportunities for students in Public Health Science to connect academic curricula to experiential learning in the workplace as an internship, Service Learning placement or general employment. Allows students to develop and work on learning objectives in workplace competencies and technical skills relevant for their course of study and career pathway. Students must work 54 hours for each unit of credit earned, in half-unit increments (27 hours), up to a maximum of 4 units. Employment can be paid or unpaid.

title: INTRODUCTION TO RECREATION AND LEISURE SERVICES
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Introduces the history, philosophy, principles, organization and direction of recreation and leisure services in the public, voluntary, private and commercial sectors. Emphasizes functions, areas, facilities, clientele and career opportunities available within the profession.

title: INTRAMURAL AND RECREATIONAL SPORT PROGRAMMING
hours: 4 hours per week: (2.50 lecture hours/1.50 lab hours)
description: Presents philosophy, foundations, policy and techniques underlying intramurals and recreational sport programming in schools, public, private and commercial recreation settings. Analyzes program design for club, informal, league and tournament formats. Discusses appropriate means for promotion, safety and risk management and participant recognition. Detailed sport program plan created.

title: RECREATION PROGRAM PLANNING
hours: 4 hours per week: (2.50 lecture hours/1.50 lab hours)
description: Presents a theoretical and practical approach to program planning, organization, implementation, and evaluation of recreation services in public, nonprofit, private, and commercial settings. Emphasis on interrelationship of needs and interests of participants with goals and objectives, physical settings and activity content. Includes planning and conducting events under direct supervision of instructor and local agency supervisor.

title: LEADERSHIP AND DIVERSE GROUPS
hours: 4 hours per week: (2.50 lecture hours/1.50 lab hours)
description: Application and development of leadership skills in the recreation setting. Emphasis on applicable leadership techniques including working with groups consisting of representatives from diverse populations such as those with disabilities or special needs, cultural and social differences, and diversity of all ages.

title: INTRODUCTION TO SOCIOLOGY
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours/ 0.00 activity hours)
description: Introduces the basic principles of sociology. Studies human social life focusing on the modern world. Emphasizes the analyses of culture, social structure, and interaction. Includes topics on socialization, crime, stratification, gender, race/ethnicity, politics, economy, family, education, religion, health care, and social change.

title: SOCIAL INSTITUTIONS
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Studies the major social institutions, both the traditional ideas of social institutions (family, education, economy, religion, and government/ politics) and contemporary ideas of social institutions (science, mass media, medicine, sports, and the military). Covers the structures and functions of social institutions. Considers major works and draws comparisons between our institutions and those of other societies.

title: SOCIAL PROBLEMS
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours/ 0.00 activity hours)
description: Examines current social problems and the sociological concepts, theories, and methods used in their analysis. Emphasizes the role of power and ideology in the definition of social problems, the causes and consequences of social problems, and the methods of intervention. Includes topics on crime, poverty, gender inequality, race/ethnic inequality, and family problems.

title: INTRODUCTION TO CRIMINOLOGY
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours/ 0.00 activity hours)
description: Introduces the basic principles of criminology including the various theories of criminal behavior and the processing of delinquency and crime including arrest, trial, detention, and release from prison.

title: INTRODUCTION TO RACE AND ETHNICITY
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours/ 0.00 activity hours)
description: Introduces students to the interdisciplinary analysis of race, ethnicity, and racism, focusing on the US American context. Examines the lived experiences and social struggles of various racial and ethnic groups. Critically examines the historical and contemporary patterns of interaction between racial and ethnic groups. Analyzes how institutions and socioeconomic, political, and cultural practices sustain or challenge racism and racial and ethnic inequality. Evaluates efforts to create a more just and equitable society at the individual, interpersonal, and societal levels.

title: INTRODUCTION TO GENDER STUDIES
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours/ 0.00 activity hours)
description: Studies the interaction of gender and society. Introduces theories of gender differentiation, stratification, and gender roles. Discusses research methodology and examines current research on gender, both within and outside the United States. Investigates how social and cultural factors (e.g., race, class) have shaped the lives of men and women as well as how they have affected their social and cultural environments. Examines the role and status of U.S. women and men within the larger social structure. Examines women and men in varying cultural settings with an emphasis on how social systems shape the roles of women and affect larger U.S. institutions.

title: INDEPENDENT STUDIES: SOCIOLOGY
hours: 1.5 to 6 hours per week: (0.00 - 0.00 lecture hours/ 1.50 - 6.00 lab hours/0.00 - 0.00 activity hours)
prereqs: The student must have completed preparatory course work in the field in which the study is to be undertaken.
description: Provides an opportunity for an in-depth study or a practicum experience by an individual student in a selected topic of sociology under the direction of an instructor.

title: SPANISH SPECIAL TOPIC
hours: 0.5 to 4 hours per week: (0.50 - 4.00 lecture hours/ 0.00 - 0.00 lab hours)
description: Examines a special topic in the field of study related to the discipline offering this course.

title: SPANISH I
hours: 5 hours per week: (5.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Presents a topic-based, introductory language acquisition course in standard contemporary Spanish, with emphasis on listening comprehension, oral interaction, culture-centered readings, and writing of basic Spanish. Social and cultural aspects of the Spanish-speaking world are presented along with the most essential structures and vocabulary. Typed written exercises and online multimedia practice activities are required.

title: SPANISH II
hours: 5 hours per week: (5.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Presents a continuation of SPAN 201 with a topiccentered, intensive practice in listening comprehension, oral interaction, and writing. Selected readings from the Hispanic world include cultural vignettes, prose selections, and poetry. Typed written exercises and online multimedia practice activities are required.

title: SPANISH III
hours: 5 hours per week: (5.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Presents a continuation of SPAN 202 incorporating a review with topic-centered intensive practice in listening comprehension, oral interaction, and paragraph writing. Selected readings from the Hispanic world include social, cultural, and historythemed vignettes, prose selections, and poetry. Typed written exercises and online multimedia practice activities are required.

title: SPANISH IV
hours: 5 hours per week: (5.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Presents an expansion of SPAN 203 focusing on 4 skills: listening , conversation, reading and presentational writing. Drawing from authentic materials, SPAN 204 is an intermediate course that provides a comprehensive grammar review, extensive oral practice and an introduction to literary concepts. Competency reflects the students' emerging ability to perform both orally and in written form with complex situations. Online multimedia practice is required and includes audio and video and extensive online resources.

title: SPANISH FOR SPANISH SPEAKERS I
hours: 4 hours per week: (4.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Develops and refines Spanish-language use for students who already have experience with the language. This course is designed for students who already speak Spanish and wish to improve and hone their skills. In addition to basic grammar and vocabulary development, this course practices writing, spelling, dialectal differences, and distinguishing between formal and informal language use.

title: SPANISH FOR SPANISH SPEAKERS II
hours: 4 hours per week: (4.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours/ 0.00 activity hours)
description: Continues to develop and refine Spanish-language use for students who already have experience with the language. This course is designed for students who already speak Spanish and wish to improve and hone their skills. In addition to more advanced grammar and vocabulary development, this course practices writing, spelling, dialectal differences, and distinguishing between formal and informal language use at a higher level.

title: INDEPENDENT STUDIES: SPANISH
hours: 1.5 to 6 hours per week: (0.00 - 0.00 lecture hours/ 1.50 - 6.00 lab hours/0.00 - 0.00 activity hours)
prereqs: The student must have completed preparatory course work in the field in which the study is to be undertaken.
description: Provides an opportunity for an in-depth study or a practicum experience by an individual student in a selected topic of Spanish under the direction of an instructor.

title: STATISTICS SUPPORT
hours: 1 hours per week: (1.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours/ 0.00 activity hours)
description: Provides just-in-time instruction and review of core prerequisite skills, competencies, and concepts necessary for success in STAT C1000, Introduction to Statistics. Includes topics from prealgebra, elementary and intermediate algebra, and the development of critical thinking skills needed for statistical analysis. Intended for students who are concurrently enrolled in STAT C1000.

title: INTRODUCTION TO STATISTICS
hours: 4 hours per week: (4.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours/ 0.00 activity hours)
prereqs: Placement as determined by the college’s multiple measures assessment process or completion of a course taught at or above the level of intermediate algebra.
description: This course is an introduction to statistical thinking and processes, including methods and concepts for discovery and decision-making using data. Topics include descriptive statistics; probability and sampling distributions; statistical inference; correlation and linear regression; analysis of variance, chi-squared, and t-tests; and application of technology for statistical analysis including the interpretation of the relevance of the statistical findings. Students apply methods and processes to applications using data from a broad range of disciplines.

title: WORK-RELATED COMMUNICATION AND COMPUTER LITERACY, LEVEL 2
hours: 2 to 3 hours per week: (2.00 - 3.00 lecture hours/0.00 - 0.00 lab hours)
description: Non Credit Develops computer skills and communication strategies for successful interaction in the workplace for intermediate level ESL learners.

title: INTRODUCTION TO HAND-HELD DEVICES
hours: 0.5 to 3 hours per week: (0.00 - 0.00 lecture hours/ 0.50 - 3.00 lab hours)
description: Non Credit Non-Credit Gradeable Course/SP Introduces practical use of a variety of handheld computer devices including music players, e-Books, Smartphones, iPods, iTouch, and iPads. The use of common PC and Mac applications to run devices, find tutorials or manuals, and identify useful settings, will also be covered. Information learned in this course will provide tips on how to use handheld devices effectively and observe protocol when determining proper use of these devices in a work environment.

title: INTRODUCTION TO FARM MAINTENANCE
hours: 1 to 6 hours per week: (0.00 - 0.00 lecture hours/1.00 - 6.00 lab hours)
description: Non Credit Non-Credit Gradeable Course/SP Provides students with an introduction to different types of agricultural operations, and a working knowledge of basic farm safety, farm, ranch and landscape construction and maintenance. Covers fundamental construction and maintenance of shelters, fencing, water systems, pastures and landscaping, and general handling and care of livestock. Covers the application of sustainable and holistic agricultural practices, and exploration of potential career paths.

title: INTRODUCTION TO LIVESTOCK IDENTIFICATION AND HANDLING
hours: 1 to 6 hours per week: (0.00 - 0.00 lecture hours/1.00 - 6.00 lab hours)
description: Non Credit Non-Credit Gradeable Course/SP Provides students with an introduction to livestock species and breeds, and a working knowledge of the fundamental requirements of animal husbandry and farm safety. Covers animal handling and restraint, general care, housing, feeding and basic health requirements. Includes identification of sustainable agricultural practices, and introduction to potential career paths.

title: INTRODUCTION TO LAND USE PLANNING AND GRAZING
hours: 1 to 6 hours per week: (0.00 - 0.00 lecture hours/1.00 - 6.00 lab hours)
description: Non Credit Non-Credit Gradeable Course/SP Provides students with an introduction to land use and grazing planning using holistic and sustainable planning methods. Covers interpreting and applying county land use regulations, operation design, planning and mapping methods, and planning targeted grazing. Emphasizes holistic management principles. Includes identification and application of sustainable and holistic agricultural practices, and exploration of potential career paths.

title: INTRODUCTION TO LIVESTOCKHEALTH
hours: 1 to 6 hours per week: (0.00 - 0.00 lecture hours/1.00 - 6.00 lab hours)
description: Non Credit Non-Credit Gradeable Course/SP Provides students with an introduction to livestock health including applicable requirements of animal husbandry and farm safety. Applies principles that address animal care, housing, and feeding as they relate to animal health. Includes the evaluation of techniques for avoiding, recognizing, and treating common health problems. Covers the application of sustainable agricultural practices, and exploration of potential career paths.

title: INTRODUCTION TO RANCH/ TARGETED GRAZING BUSINESS
hours: 1 to 6 hours per week: (0.00 - 0.00 lecture hours/1.00 - 6.00 lab hours)
description: Non Credit Non-Credit Gradeable Course/SP Provides students with an introduction to basic business practices relating to ranch and/or targeted grazing enterprises. Students will identify requirements for a business plan, contract and legal options, cost estimation, and price setting for services, insurance costs, advertising, and public relations programs.

title: INTRODUCTION TOLEATHERWORK -- BASICS IN SCULPTING ANDSTRAP WORK
hours: 1 to 6 hours per week: (0.00 - 0.00 lecture hours/1.00 - 6.00 lab hours/0.00 - 0.00 activity hours)
description: Non Credit Non-Credit Gradeable Course/SP Provides students with an introduction to basic leatherworking. Covers use of correct terminology, fundamental selection and safe usage of tools, creation of patterns, identification and selection of appropriate materials, fastening and construction techniques, and construction of simple projects. Repeatable: None Times

title: INTERMEDIATE LEATHERWORK: CONSTRUCTION OF MULTIPIECE DESIGNS
hours: 1 to 6 hours per week: (0.00 - 0.00 lecture hours/1.00 - 6.00 lab hours)
description: Non Credit Non-Credit Gradeable Course/SP Provides students with practical experience planning and constructing intermediate leatherworking projects. Covers selection and use of tools, identification and selection of appropriate materials and construction of multi-piece leatherworking projects. Requires students to identify and source appropriate materials and tools and estimate the cost of planning and constructing leatherworking projects. Explores potential career paths. Repeatable: None Times ## VOCE 566C ADVANCED LEATHERWORK: Non Credit Non-Credit Gradeable Course/SP Provides students with practical experience in a variety of advanced leatherworking processes and projects. Covers advanced selection and use of leather stamping, sculpting, cutting and punching tools, and the use of glue, snaps and stitching as fasteners. Includes identification, selection and use of appropriate materials such as cow hides and other natural and human-made products, sourcing materials and tools, estimating the cost of, planning and construction of complex leatherworking projects. Explores the historical-cultural significance and environmental impact of leatherwork and the leather industry.

title: PRACTICAL LEATHER REPAIR
description: Non Credit Non-Credit Gradeable Course/SP Provides students experienced in leatherworking with practical experience in a variety of leather repair processes and projects. Covers methods of leather repair, selection and use of tools, identification and selection of appropriate materials, sourcing materials and tools and estimating the cost of and planning advanced leatherworking and leather repair projects. Explores different styles of saddles and saddle-making.

Covers identification and safe use of tools, selection of appropriate materials, and application of fundamental techniques to complete simple projects.

hours: 1 to 6 hours per week: (0.00 - 0.00 lecture hours/1.00 - 6.00 lab hours/0.00 - 0.00 activity hours) Non

This course develops photo editing and basic internet skills for business or personal use.

description: Non Credit Non-Credit Gradeable Course/SP Designed for students with limited experience with computers, this course introduces how to perform basic computer tasks. Includes how to turn a computer on and off correctly, send and receive email, navigate the internet, open and save a file, and use computer terminology. Course may be taught bilingually.

Instructor-led guided exploration activities will include Help, windows navigation and management, file management, desktop customization, and other Windows Operating system tools and applications.

description: Non-Credit Gradeable Course/SP Provides instruction in correct finger and wrist placement, and keyboard reaches for typing and texting. Refreshes skills in keyboarding, increases speed, and provides techniques and strategies to prevent carpal tunnel syndrome. Individualized instruction allows students to work at own pace. May be taught bilingually.

title: BASIC WORD PROCESSING

description: Non-Credit Gradeable Course/SP Provides instruction in successfully navigating the computer screen and composing and editing a short document. Class pace allows students to become comfortable with the computer and editing techniques.

title: BASIC OUTLOOK

description: Non Credit Non-Credit Gradeable Course/SP Introduces skills which are needed to stay up to date at home and at work through the use of Microsoft Outlook. Covers the basics of how to connect with colleagues, customers, family and friends. Topics include writing and searching email, organizing work tasks, and using the calendar to share information with others.

title: BASIC SPREADSHEETS FOR BEGINNERS
hours: 1 hours per week: (0.00 lecture hours/1.00 lab hours) Non
description: Non-Credit Gradeable Course/SP Introduces basic concepts and functions of Microsoft Excel. Topics include the basics of creating a spreadsheet, using formulas and functions, and creating charts.

description: hours) Non Credit Non-Credit Gradeable Course/SP Introduces the basic concepts and characteristics of Microsoft Excel. Course topics will explore various uses of spreadsheets. description: Non Credit Non-Credit Gradeable Course/SP Introduces key functions and skills which are used for document creation in Microsoft Word. title: CALIFORNIA CONSERVATION AWARENESS-AN INTRODUCTION
hours: 1 hours per week: (1.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours) Non
description: Non-Credit Gradeable Course/SP Provides students with an overview of the concepts and current status of biological conservation of California ecosystems. This course explores the biodiversity, food web interactions, natural resources and ecosystem services within the redwood/coastal, chaparral/oak woodland, Sierra/ pine, and urban systems, with emphasis placed on their status, impacts and solutions. This course is designed to benefit to those actively participating in hands-on conservation efforts throughout the state.

title: CALIFORNIA CONSERVATION EMPLOYMENT
hours: 1 hours per week: (1.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours) Non
description: Non-Credit Gradeable Course/SP Provides students seeking employment in conservation-related fields with an overview of the safety, workplace, job search and preparation skills through local and regional employment opportunities.

hours: 0.5 hours per week: (0.50 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Non Credit Non-Credit Gradeable Course/SP Presents and applies the scientific principles of fitness and nutrition for a healthful lifestyle. description: Presents and applies the scientific principles of fitness and nutrition for a healthy lifestyle. Upon completion of the course, the student will be able to continue applying and implementing the fitness principles, wellness parameters, and fitness guidelines into their personal lifestyles.

title: COMMERCIAL DRIVER TRAINING-PERMIT PREPARATION
hours: 1 to 8 hours per week: (1.00 - 8.00 lecture hours/0.00 - 0.00 lab hours)
description: Non Credit Non-Credit Gradeable Course/SP Enables students to become familiar with regulations governing the operation of commercial vehicles and safe operational practices. This course follows state and federal guidelines for commercial driver training programs. Participation in this course does not guarantee students will earn their Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP). Upon completion of this course students must pass the written Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP) test at a California DMV office to earn their CLP.

title: COMMERCIAL DRIVER TRAINING:RANGE OPERATIONS
hours: 1 to 6 hours per week: (0.50 - 3.00 lecture hours/0.50 - 3.00 lab hours)
description: Non Credit Non-Credit Gradeable Course/SP Prepares students for the range operations section of the California CMV License test. Students will practice moving forward, backing, parallel parking, backing into a dock, and other operations typical of a commercial driver. Students will also demonstrate proficiency performing pre-trip inspections and the required air brake system test. Students must have a California Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP) prior to starting this class. Instructors (at their discretion) may allow students with a CLP test scheduled to start the course, but students will not be allowed to operate CMVs until they have passed the CLP test.

title: COMMERCIAL DRIVING TRAINING -ON ROAD SKILLS
hours: 0.5 to 8 hours per week: (0.00 - 0.00 lecture hours/ 0.50 - 8.00 lab hours)
description: Non-Credit Gradeable Course/SP Provides students with instruction and practice in safe Commercial Motor Vehicle (CMV) operation, including driving a CMV with an instructor on public and private roads. Students must have a California Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP) prior to enrolling in this course.

title: BASIC WATER TREATMENT
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours/ 0.00 activity hours)
description: Prepares the student to take the California's State Water Treatment Plant Operator, Grade 1 or Grade 2 exam. Includes the study of plant operation, water sources and treatment, reservoir management, coagulation and flocculation, sedimentation, filtration, disinfection, taste and odor control, and corrosion control.

title: WATER DISTRIBUTION SYSTEMS
hours: 3 hours per week: (3.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours/ 0.00 activity hours)
description: Prepares the student to take the California's State Water Distribution Plant Operator, Grade 1 exam. Provides an understanding of the basic operational and maintenance concepts of water distribution systems. Develops the ability to analyze and solve problems such as tastes and odors, corrosion damage, and system failures when they occur.

title: SURVEY OF WELDING
hours: 4 hours per week: (1.00 lecture hours/3.00 lab hours)
description: Provides welding process instruction to include Shielded Metal Arc Welding (SMAW), Oxy Acetylene Welding (OAW), Gas Metal Arc Welding (GMAW), Gas Tungsten Arc Welding (GTAW), and Flux Core Arc Welding (FCAW). Also includes instruction in Oxy Fuel Cutting (OFC) and Plasma Arc Cutting (PAC). Safety instruction will include industry standard Job Safety Analysis (JSA) with material from ANSI Z49.1.

title: WELDING TECHNOLOGY SPECIAL TOPIC
hours: 0.5 to 4 hours per week: (0.50 - 4.00 lecture hours/ 0.00 - 0.00 lab hours)
description: Examines a special topic in the field of study related to the discipline offering this course.

description: Provides an opportunity for in-depth study or practicum experience by an individual student in a selected topic in the Welding Technology area with support and direction from an instructor.

title: WORK EXPERIENCE IN WELDING

description: Provides opportunities for students in Welding to connect academic curricula to experiential learning in the workplace as an internship, Service Learning placement or general employment. Allows students to develop and work on learning objectives in workplace competencies and technical skills relevant for their course of study and career pathway. Students must work 54 hours for each unit of credit earned, in half-unit increments (27 hours), up to a maximum of 4 units. Employment can be paid or unpaid. Repeatable: 3 Times

title: BASIC WELDING
hours: 6 hours per week: (2.00 lecture hours/4.00 lab hours)
description: Provides basic instruction in oxyacetylene and shielded metal arc welding. Begins with the fundamentals and quickly progresses through intermediate skills for welding steel. Includes information on cutting, braze welding, metallurgy, vertical arc welding and non-ferrous welding. Emphasizes the development of good manipulative welding skills for joining steel in the flat and horizontal positions.

title: ADVANCED WELDING
hours: 6 hours per week: (2.00 lecture hours/4.00 lab hours)
description: Continues WELD 270A with emphasis placed on vertical and overhead welding with the shielded metal arc processes. Includes instruction on air carbon arc gouging, flux core arc welding, and development of welding procedures and techniques.

title: WELDING: GMAW & GTAW
hours: 6 hours per week: (2.00 lecture hours/4.00 lab hours)
description: Focuses on using the Gas Tungsten Arc Welding (GTAW), Gas Metal Arc Welding (GMAW) and Flux Core Arc Welding (FCAW) processes to produce complex welded joints on ferrous and nonferrous materials in a variety of positions.

title: METALLURGY
hours: 5 hours per week: (2.00 lecture hours/3.00 lab hours)
description: Emphasizes the mechanical and physical properties of ferrous and non-ferrous metals. Includes preparation and inspection of metal samples and manufacturing and forming processes.

title: BLUEPRINT READING AND INDUSTRY PRACTICES
hours: 6 hours per week: (2.00 lecture hours/4.00 lab hours)
description: Provides students with instruction and experience with structural, architectural and shop blueprints commonly utilized in the welding industry. Interpretation, drawing, and application of skills will be applied to determining job cost, material acquisition and project construction.

title: WELDING POWER
hours: 6 hours per week: (2.00 lecture hours/4.00 lab hours)
description: Applies principles of selection, maintenance, diagnostics and repair of various welding power supplies and external drive mechanisms. Includes instruction and hands on experiences in electrical principles as they pertain to machine selection, installation, operation and maintenance. Manual, semiautomatic and automatic equipment will be included as focus topics for this course.

title: METAL FABRICATION
hours: 6 hours per week: (2.00 lecture hours/4.00 lab hours)
description: Prepares the student to meet industry standards through the design and construct of major projects through the instruction on manufacturing processes, and current industry production techniques. Includes development of a project proposal in which students develop drawings, budgets, cut lists and bills of materials.

title: STRUCTURAL STEEL WELDING CERTIFICATION
hours: 6 hours per week: (2.00 lecture hours/4.00 lab hours)
description: Continues WELD 270B. Prepares the student to meet industry standards in shielded metal arc welding on plate steel. Includes performance and procedure qualification, workmanship, techniques, inspection. Provides opportunity for certification to the American Welding Society D1.1 Structural Welding Code.

title: PIPE WELDING CERTIFICATION
hours: 6 hours per week: (2.00 lecture hours/4.00 lab hours)
description: Prepares the student to meet industry standards in Shielded Metal Arc Welding (SMAW) on plate and pipe, as well as introduces Gas Tungsten Arc Welding (GTAW) on pipe. Includes workmanship and pipe fitting techniques, providing opportunity for certification to the American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME) Section IX Boiler and Pressure Vessel code.

title: WORK EXPERIENCE - COHORT
hours: 2 to 12.5 hours per week: (0.50 - 0.50 lecture hours/ 0.00 - 0.00 lab hours/1.50 - 12.00 work experience hours)
description: Provides opportunities to connect academic curricula to experiential learning in the workplace as an internship, Service Learning placement or general employment. Allows students to develop and work on learning objectives in essential job search skills, workplace competencies, and technical skills relevant for their course of study and career pathway. Includes modules on job search skills, workplace competencies, and experiential learning strategies as well as participation in group discussions, representing one-half lecture unit, and must work 54 hours for each additional unit of credit earned, in half-unit increments (27 hours). Students may earn a maximum of 4 units for Work Experience in addition to the one-half lecture unit. Employment can be paid or unpaid. Repeatable: 3 Times

title: WORKPLACE READINESS PREPARATION
hours: 1 hours per week: (1.00 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Prepares students to successfully pursue and perform in a job, internship, Service Learning placement or Work Experience course. Requires completion of modules on job search skills, workplace competencies, and experiential learning strategies.

title: PERSONALIZED CAREER PLANNING
hours: 0.5 hours per week: (0.50 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Non Credit Non-Credit Gradeable Course/SP Focuses on the assessment of individuals' strengths, interests, values, personality and abilities in the context of career and education planning. Guided discussion and activities will help to improve participants decision-making skills by exploring their own decision-making styles and applying specific decision making models to their careerplanning process.

title: STRATEGIC JOB SEARCH
hours: 0.5 hours per week: (0.50 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Non Credit Non-Credit Gradeable Course/SP Introduces skills and knowledge students need to develop and implement a strategic career and job search plan. Different sources of occupational information and how to utilize this information in the career planning and job search process will be presented and discussed.

title: PLANNING YOUR NEXT CAREER
hours: 0.5 hours per week: (0.50 lecture hours/0.00 lab hours)
description: Non Credit Non-Credit Gradeable Course/SP Designed for older adults who wish to explore new work and career opportunities. Students develop work-related goals, examine their work histories, identify marketable employment skills, and identify local employment resources and supports.
